To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the recovery of corals after a cyclone is driven by the rapid recruitment of small colonies, which overtook surviving colonies within 2 years of disturbance, and the recovery of coral communities was dominated by the small colonies.
the recovery of coral abundance following a severe tropical storm on the inshore GBR was driven by the establishment of new populations and the growth of surviving populations.

(1) coral recovery is a key process in determining the resilience of coral communities following disturbance; (2) colony abundance and size-distribution are useful metrics to understand the mechanisms involved in the recovery of coral communities following cyclone disturbance; (3) the number of small colonies increased substantially during the 5-year study period, driving coral recovery; (4) the total number of coral communities 5 years post-cyclone was between 73 and122% of pre-disturbance levels
In summary, our research is concerned with
the dynamics of coral communities following a severe disturbance.
the recovery of coral reefs after disturbance and how this recovery is influenced by the availability of coral larvae.
understanding the mechanisms underlying the early-stage recovery of coral reefs following a severe tropical disturbance.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the recovery of coral communities on the inshore GBR following the 2011 tropical cyclone was primarily driven by the recruitment of coral larvae and the establishment of newly settled colonies.
the early-phase recovery dynamics of the coral community on the inshore GBR were characterized by rapid recruitment and growth of coral colonies and the establishment of new coral populations.

coral recovery (the restoration to abundance and composition of the coral community) is a key process determining the resilience of coral reef ecosystems, and that the mechanisms underlying this recovery process are complex and involve a combination of factors including coral recruitment and growth.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
coral recovery following a major disturbance is driven by the establishment of new colonies, which is a function of larval supply and recruitment processes.
the recovery of coral communities following a major disturbance is primarily driven by the rapid recruitment of new coral populations.
the recovery of coral communities following disturbance is driven by recruitment and growth of coral populations, which is a key process in determining the resilience of coral reef ecosystems.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the recovery of coral communities following a severe disturbance event is a dynamic process that is driven by the recruitment of new coral colonies.
coral reefs are dynamic and that coral populations can recover from major disturbance events.
the initial recovery of the coral community is driven primarily by the establishment of new populations, and the abundance of small colonies is a key indicator of coral community recovery.
